name: xa
why: A 6502 cross assembler; a gateway into writing code for classic 8-bit machines like the NES and Apple II.

brief.what_it_is: xa (xa65) is Andre Fachat's open-source, portable 6502 cross assembler, now maintained by Cameron Kaiser. It takes 6502-family assembly source and produces binary output, with a C-like preprocessor, a rich expression syntax, and pseudo-ops. It targets NMOS 6502 variants, CMOS 65C02 and Rockwell R65C02, and the 65816. It can emit plain binary or o65 relocatable objects, and it includes a linker and relocation tools. The package ships several executables: xa, file65, ldo65, printcbm, reloc65 and uncpk. Its companion disassembler dxa is distributed separately as alpha software.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no single mission statement. Andre Fachat's history says he wrote xa to build programs for his self-built CS/A65 computer, and he added o65 objects and a linker in 1996 when he needed to push that homebrew OS further.
brief.how_it_works: xa is described as a two-pass assembler. It reads mnemonics and directives, and it emits machine code for the selected CPU type. Relocatable output goes to o65 objects, which the linker and relocation suite (ldo65, reloc65) can combine later. Relocation mode can leave undefined labels unresolved so they can be linked at a later time.

brief.install_notes: The homepage says xa should compile out of the box on most Unix-like systems and on other systems with an ANSI C compiler. It points to a README.1st for detailed build instructions, which I did not read. It was tested on AIX, Linux/ppc64le, Mac OS X on PowerPC, Intel and Apple silicon, and NetBSD on macppc and mac68k. The source tarball is xa-2.4.1.tar.gz. dxa is a separate tarball, dxa-0.1.5.tar.gz, and its readme covers its installation. No accounts, special hardware or runtimes are mentioned.
brief.standout: xa is a long-lived, full-featured cross assembler that bundles an o65 relocatable object format, a linker, and relocation tools, which most small 6502 assemblers lack. It also has a deliberate design goal for dxa: a disassemble-then-reassemble round trip should reproduce the original binary byte for byte.
brief.status: maintained. The latest release is xa 2.4.1 from 5 March 2024. The page says bug reports should now go to Cameron Kaiser, the current maintainer. dxa's latest release is 0.1.5 from 25 March 2022. I did not check a commit log or the repository, so I cannot speak to recent commit activity.
brief.caveats: The homepage does not mention the NES or the Apple II. The scout note's framing is an inference, and the page only names NMOS, CMOS and 65816 CPU families. Version 2.4.0 changed behaviour and may break edge cases from 2.3 and earlier, and features deprecated in 2.3 were removed. The -M option and the printcbm tool are deprecated; the page points to VICE's petcat as the replacement for printcbm. dxa is alpha software and the page warns to expect bugs; it does not yet support the 65816. Relevant is the claim that xa builds on most Unix-like systems, and the homepage does not mention Windows. The package is GPL v2.
quotes: xa is a high-speed, two-pass portable cross-assembler.
xa should compile out of the box on just about any Unix or Unixy thing, and will probably compile on other systems that support ANSI C as well.
Please consider it to be alpha software only and expect bugs.
